accountUsageLimit.title: Account usage limit
accountUsageLimit.description: Shared stop for Claude, Codex, Cursor, and Kiro when included account usage is exhausted.

stopTurns.title: Stop turns at 100% usage
stopTurns.description: When a provider reports included usage at 100%, block new turns and background AI for that provider so extra credits are not spent. Turns that are already running can still finish. Turn this off to keep working on overage.

trustedApprovals.title: Trusted Approvals
trustedApprovals.description: Approvals marked as always allowed. Bash entries are stored as command prefixes instead of trusting every shell command.
trustedApprovals.empty: No trusted approvals yet. Use approve and always allow from an approval prompt to add one.

claudeRuntime.title: Claude Runtime Controls
claudeRuntime.description: Permission, sandbox, thinking, and subagent progress behavior passed into each Claude turn.

modePreset.description: Apply a recommended Claude autonomy preset. Editing the fields below can move the card into Custom.
modePreset.active: {{preset}} is active. Reapply a preset any time to restore its full permission and sandbox combination.
modePreset.custom: Custom is active. The current Claude permission and sandbox combination does not match a built-in preset.

permissionMode.title: Permission Mode
permissionMode.description: Controls how aggressively Claude asks for permission during a chat turn. Claude CLI sessions always launch in `auto`.

guide.title: Claude Permission Mode
guide.summary: This is the main autonomy dial for Claude turns.

default.description: Use Claude's standard permission behavior without asking Stave to bias the mode.
default.example: Pick this when you want the least opinionated baseline and do not need a special workflow.

acceptEdits.description: Good default for normal coding sessions where edits are expected but you still want guardrails.
acceptEdits.example: Use this for day-to-day feature work, bug fixes, and iterative patching.

bypassPermissions.description: Most autonomous Claude path. Pair it carefully with permission-skipping controls.
bypassPermissions.example: Use this only when you trust the task scope and want Claude to move with minimal interruption.

dontAsk.description: Tell Claude not to stop for interactive permission questions during the turn.
dontAsk.example: Useful for fast local workflows when you want fewer pauses but do not want plan mode.

auto.description: Let Claude choose the most appropriate permission behavior for the turn. Claude CLI sessions require Claude Code 2.1.71+ for this mode; older CLI builds fall back to `default`.
auto.example: Good when your workload shifts between analysis, coding, and light automation throughout the day.

sandbox.title: Sandbox Enabled
sandbox.description: Wrap Claude tool execution in its sandbox configuration.

unsandboxedCommands.title: Allow Unsandboxed Commands
unsandboxedCommands.description: Controls whether Claude may fall back to commands outside the sandbox.

credentialFiles.title: Protected Credential Files
credentialFiles.description: Comma-separated file paths Claude's sandbox must deny as credentials. Enter paths only, never secret contents.

credentialVariables.title: Protected Credential Variables
credentialVariables.description: Comma-separated environment variable names Claude's sandbox must deny. Enter names only; values never belong here.

settingSources.title: Setting Sources
settingSources.description: Controls which Claude filesystem setting layers are loaded. `project` is required for CLAUDE.md and project slash commands.

guide.title: Claude Setting Sources
guide.summary: These layers decide which Claude configuration files and commands participate in each turn.
guide.tooltip: What each Claude setting source does

project.label: Project
project.description: Load repo-level Claude settings such as `CLAUDE.md` and project-native slash commands.

local.label: Local
local.description: Load machine-local or workspace-local Claude settings from the runtime environment.

user.label: User
user.description: Load your user-wide Claude settings and personal defaults.

taskBudget.title: Task Budget (Tokens)
taskBudget.description: Advisory token budget sent to Claude so it can pace tool use and wrap up earlier. Use `0` to disable.

guide.title: Claude Thinking Mode
guide.summary: Thinking controls whether Claude spends extra effort on explicit reasoning before answering.

adaptive.label: Adaptive
adaptive.description: Claude decides when deeper thinking is worth the extra latency.
adaptive.example: Best default when some turns are simple and others need real analysis.

enabled.description: Always ask for explicit thinking, even on simpler prompts.
enabled.example: Use this when you prioritize careful reasoning over response speed.

disabled.description: Prefer direct answers without extra thinking overhead.
disabled.example: Useful for tiny edits, routing, or repetitive low-risk tasks.

guide.title: Claude Effort
guide.summary: Higher effort spends more model budget on reasoning and usually increases latency.

low.example: Good for short questions, quick rewrites, and simple code edits.

medium.description: Balanced reasoning depth for most day-to-day tasks.
medium.example: Use this as the default if you frequently switch between analysis and implementation.

high.description: Spend more effort on difficult debugging, design, or review work.
high.example: Useful for tricky bugs, architecture questions, or larger refactors.

xhigh.description: Go deeper than `high` when the Claude model supports it, with a larger latency cost.
xhigh.example: Best for complex root-cause analysis or hard multi-step implementation planning.

max.description: Highest deliberation and the most latency.
max.example: Reserve this for genuinely hard tasks where accuracy matters more than speed.

agentProgressSummaries.title: Agent Progress Summaries
agentProgressSummaries.description: Enables Claude SDK `task_progress.summary` updates for running subagents.

promptSuggestions.title: Prompt Suggestions
promptSuggestions.description: Offers follow-up prompt chips after each completed turn. Costs one extra lightweight request per turn on top of the turn itself; background lanes never request suggestions.

forwardSubagentText.title: Forward Subagent Text
forwardSubagentText.description: Streams nested subagent transcript text instead of only subagent progress heartbeats.

fileCheckpointing.title: File Checkpointing
fileCheckpointing.description: Enables Claude SDK file checkpoints so changed files can be rewound by session controls.

forkSession.title: Fork Resumed Session
forkSession.description: When resuming a Claude session, fork to a new session instead of continuing the previous one.

strictMcpConfig.title: Strict MCP Config
strictMcpConfig.description: Only use MCP servers passed by Stave and explicitly configured SDK agents.

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: Comma- or newline-separated Claude skill names. Use `all` to enable every discovered skill.

pluginPaths.title: Plugin Paths
pluginPaths.description: Comma- or newline-separated local Claude plugin directories. Stave owns MCP discovery for these plugins.

mainAgent.title: Main Agent
mainAgent.description: Optional Claude agent name from settings or loaded plugins for the main conversation.

fallbackModels.title: Fallback Models
fallbackModels.description: Comma-separated Claude fallback models used when the primary model is overloaded or unavailable. Opus 5.5 automatically falls back to Opus 4.8 when left blank.

resumeAt.title: Resume At Message
resumeAt.description: Optional Claude assistant message UUID for partial resume from a previous session.

codexRuntime.title: Codex Runtime Controls
codexRuntime.description: Per-turn Codex file access, approvals, network, reasoning, and search settings.

modePreset.description: Apply a recommended Codex autonomy preset. Editing the fields below can move the card into Custom.
modePreset.active: {{preset}} is active. Reapply a preset any time to restore its full file access, approval, and network combination.
modePreset.custom: Custom is active. The current Codex file-access and approval combination does not match a built-in preset.

networkAccess.title: Network Access
networkAccess.description: Controls whether Codex may use networked capabilities during a turn.

guide.title: Codex File Access
guide.summary: This setting controls where Codex can read and write on disk.

readOnly.description: Read and inspect only. Codex should not mutate files.
readOnly.example: Use this for reviews, audits, repo exploration, or planning.

workspaceWrite.description: Allow edits inside the current workspace and writable roots.
workspaceWrite.example: Recommended App Server-style starting point for normal local work.

dangerFullAccess.description: Remove most filesystem restrictions and allow broad mutation.
dangerFullAccess.example: Use this only for trusted automation that truly needs unrestricted file access.

guide.title: Codex Approvals
guide.summary: Approval policy controls when Codex pauses to ask before acting.

untrusted.description: Only pause for actions the runtime treats as untrusted or higher risk.
untrusted.example: Recommended App Server-style baseline when you want fewer routine approval pauses.

never.description: Do not stop for approval prompts. Codex proceeds directly.
never.example: Good for trusted local workflows when you want continuous execution.

onRequest.description: Pause when approval is needed and ask you to confirm.
onRequest.example: Use this when you want more explicit checkpoints than the default low-friction setup.

onFailure.description: Let Codex retry with approval only after an operation fails without it.
onFailure.example: Useful when you want low-friction execution but still want a recovery path for blocked commands.

appToolApprovals.title: App Tool Approvals
appToolApprovals.description: Controls App and MCP tools separately from shell command approvals.

guide.title: Codex App Tool Approvals
guide.summary: This controls approval prompts for connected App and MCP tools, not shell commands or sandbox permissions.
guide.note: `writes` trusts each tool's read-only annotation; it is not a security boundary.

inherit.label: Inherit
inherit.description: Keep the user's Codex config for App and MCP tool approvals.
inherit.example: Use this when Codex config.toml is the source of truth.

auto.description: Let Codex choose when an App or MCP tool needs approval.

prompt.label: Prompt
prompt.description: Ask before every App or MCP tool call.

writes.label: Writes
writes.description: Ask only for tools not marked read-only by their tool annotation.
writes.example: This is an approval hint, not a filesystem or network sandbox boundary.

approve.label: Approve
approve.description: Approve App and MCP tool calls without prompting.

guide.title: Codex Reasoning Effort
guide.summary: Higher effort gives Codex more room to reason, but it also tends to slow the turn down.

minimal.description: Shortest reasoning path and the least latency.
minimal.example: Use this for rote edits, quick file lookups, or tiny transformations.

low.example: Good for small implementation tasks and direct answers.

medium.description: Balanced depth for everyday coding and debugging.
medium.example: Recommended default when task difficulty varies.

high.description: More deliberate reasoning for harder or more ambiguous tasks.
high.example: Use this for larger bug hunts, refactors, or multi-step design questions.

xhigh.description: Deepest reasoning budget and the highest latency cost.
xhigh.example: Reserve this for genuinely complex work where you want Codex to think much longer.

max.description: Highest deliberation on the GPT-5.6 effort scale, above `xhigh`.
max.example: Reserve this for hard multi-step implementation or debugging work where accuracy matters more than speed.

ultra.description: The deepest reasoning budget Codex offers and the highest latency cost. Not every model accepts this tier (e.g. GPT-5.6 Luna caps at `max`).
ultra.example: Reserve this for the hardest frontier-model tasks where you want Codex to think as long as possible.

reasoningSummary.title: Reasoning Summary
reasoningSummary.description: Codex config for model-side reasoning summaries when supported.

guide.title: Codex Reasoning Summary
guide.summary: This controls how much reasoning summary Codex should try to return when the model supports it.

auto.description: Let Codex decide whether and how much reasoning summary to return.
auto.example: Good default when you want Stave to adapt across different models.

concise.label: Concise
concise.description: Request a short summary of model-side reasoning.
concise.example: Useful when you want quick visibility without a lot of extra text.

detailed.label: Detailed
detailed.description: Request a fuller reasoning summary when the model supports it.
detailed.example: Use this when you care about understanding why Codex chose a path.

none.description: Do not request a reasoning summary.
none.example: Useful when you want the leanest possible UI output.

summarySupport.title: Summary Support
summarySupport.description: Override Codex capability detection when a model supports reasoning summaries but the runtime cannot infer it.

guide.title: Reasoning Summary Capability Override
guide.summary: Only touch this when automatic capability detection is wrong.
guide.tooltip: How reasoning summary support override works

auto.description: Let Stave and the Codex runtime infer whether reasoning summaries are supported.
auto.example: Start here unless you know a model is being detected incorrectly.

enabled.description: Force-enable reasoning summary support even if automatic detection misses it.
enabled.example: Use this when a model supports summaries but the runtime does not infer it correctly.

disabled.example: Use this if a model claims support but returns noisy or broken summary behavior.

rawReasoning.title: Raw Reasoning
rawReasoning.description: Shows low-level reasoning traces when Codex emits them.

webSearch.title: Web Search
webSearch.description: Default is `cached`, which allows lower-volatility search without turning on live external lookup.

guide.title: Codex Web Search
guide.summary: Use this when Codex needs outside knowledge rather than only repo-local context.

cached.label: Cached
cached.description: Allow search in a lower-volatility mode when cached results are available.
cached.example: Recommended default when you want some search help without always relying on live web access.

disabled.description: Do not let Codex use web search.
disabled.example: Best when you want fully local reasoning or reproducible offline behavior.

indexed.label: Indexed
indexed.description: Use Codex's indexed search corpus without requesting a live fetch for every query.
indexed.example: Use this for broad documentation discovery when the selected Codex runtime is 0.142 or newer.

live.label: Live
live.description: Allow live web search when the task needs current external information.
live.example: Use this for latest docs, breaking API changes, or recent news-style facts.

delegationSection.title: Delegated tasks
delegationSection.description: An agent can hand work to a new Stave task with its own conversation and permissions, recorded on the run ledger and kept across restarts. There is no switch to turn on: ask the agent to delegate, and this card shows whether it can.

availability.heading: Availability
availability.note: Delegation reaches the model as Local MCP tools, so a task can only start subagents while that server is running.

asking.heading: Asking for one, and what you can specify
asking.body: There is no button: delegation happens when an agent callsstave_delegate_taskduring its turn, so you steer it by asking — for example “get a read-only second opinion on this plan from Codex at high effort”. Only the prompt is required: anything a delegation leaves out follows this task's provider, effort and permissions, and the child runs one turn in this workspace. Settings holds no global default for any of it.
asking.controls: Once a delegation starts, its child appears in the task's turn activity with Open, Follow-up, Stop, Detach and Retry controls.

parameters.access: read-only for second opinions, reviews and research: the child cannot change files, needs no approvals, and runs beside other work in the same workspace. Defaults to inherit: this task's permissions on the same provider, otherwise that provider's user settings.
parameters.provider: Claude or Codex. Defaults to this task's provider.
parameters.lifecycle: Defaults to one-turn, which ends the delegation when the child's first turn ends; detached keeps the child open until stopped.
parameters.workspace: Defaults to the same workspace. A new worktree on its own branch keeps edits isolated.
parameters.model: Defaults to the child provider's default model.
parameters.effort: low → max (Codex also has ultra), clamped to what the child's model accepts. Defaults to this task's effort on the same provider, otherwise medium. A bounded brief often does better on a cheaper model at high effort.
